research_limitations: WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted (200/200) partway through, and the outbound HTTPS gateway policy-denied CONNECT to every commerce and collector host attempted (www.ebay.com, www.mercari.com, www.hottopic.com, boxlunch.com, shop.universalorlando.com, harrypottershop.com, harrypotter.com, paperhouseproductions.com, conquestjournal.com, elbenwald.com, merchoid.com, theshopthatmustnotbenamed.co.uk, hedgehogscorner.com, harrypotter.fandom.com). No page was successfully fetched. Consequently NO eBay sold comps were obtained for any item: every market_low_usd / market_median_usd / market_high_usd is null and every price_confidence is "low". URLs in source_urls are real URLs returned by WebSearch together with page-summary content for those URLs; they were NOT directly fetched. No product name, SKU, edition size, or price has been invented.

pins.name: Luna Lovegood Spectrespecs enamel pin
pins.property: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
pins.notes: Design identity is certain — Luna's Spectrespecs are unmistakable. The specific product is NOT pinned down: at least three different licensed Spectrespecs pins exist (a Hot Topic 'Harry Potter Luna Lovegood Spectrespecs Enamel Pin', a Loungefly 'Luna Lovegood With Spectrespecs' exclusive pin dated 2021, and an Elbenwald-distributed 'Luna Lovegood Spectrespecs Pin'), plus Funko Pop!-sized pins and many Etsy fan versions. The board example has flat hard-enamel lenses (pink/white swirl left, blue swirl right) rather than the transparent-enamel or 3D-molded lenses described for the Funko version, so the Funko pin is likely ruled out. Cannot distinguish between the Hot Topic and Loungefly/Elbenwald versions from the photo.
pins.board_note: Top-left corner of the board. Pink/magenta cat-eye frames with fringed comb-like outer edges; left lens white-and-pink spiral, right lens blue-and-white spiral. Roughly 40mm wide.

pins.name: Defence Against the Dark Arts pin badge
pins.notes: Strong match to a documented officially licensed pin: a circular badge with a bright green fist-and-wand icon ringed by 'Defence Against the Dark Arts / Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry' plus a list of charms, hexes and creatures, made of zinc alloy and epoxy resin, approx. 3cm x 4cm (the 40mm dimension includes the wand overhanging both sides), supplied on a Harry Potter branded backing card. The board example shows exactly this: green fist, green wand crossing the full width, small dense text block below the fist. Manufacturer not confirmed — the retailers carrying it (The Shop That Must Not Be Named, Merchoid) are UK sellers of Half Moon Bay / Warner Bros. licensed goods, but I could not load either page to confirm the brand or SKU. size_mm is taken from the retailer description, not measured.
pins.board_note: Top row, second from left. Round very dark navy/black disc, glossy green clenched fist in the centre with a green wand crossing horizontally and protruding past the rim on both sides; 'DEFENCE AGAINST' arcs over the top, 'THE DARK ARTS' across the bottom, with a small block of fine text under the fist.

pins.name: Owl Post pin (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED to a product. 'Owl Post' is the wizarding postal service and the name of shops in both Hogsmeade (Universal's Islands of Adventure) and Diagon Alley (Universal Studios Florida), so a Universal park pin is the leading hypothesis, but I found no Universal or other retailer listing matching this specific design. Searches surfaced only unrelated Hedwig-and-letter pins (Seven Times Six / Target / Amazon HPPB1746), a ClipClock 'HP Owl Post Service Badge' costume accessory, and Etsy handmade 'owl post' pins. Because Etsy carries many unlicensed fan versions of Owl Post artwork, unlicensed-fan-pin status cannot be ruled out for this item, though the raised gold filigree border and gold banner-with-black-lettering construction read as commercial die-struck manufacture rather than typical fan print-on-demand.
pins.board_note: Top row, third from left. Round pin, roughly 40mm. Black field with a front-facing brown/greyish-brown textured owl perched on a black branch; heavy raised antique-gold filigree of spirals runs around the whole rim; gold banner across the bottom reads 'OWL POST' in black serif capitals.

pins.name: Platform 9¾ station sign pin (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED to a product. The King's Cross Platform 9¾ sign is one of the most heavily reproduced Harry Potter motifs and appears as a pin from dozens of licensees and countless unlicensed sellers, so I will not attach a product name without a matching listing. The gold-outlined maroon roundel-with-banner construction here matches licensed die-struck enamel manufacture. No comparable listing was located before the search budget ran out.
pins.board_note: Second row far left. Deep maroon/oxblood enamel London Underground-style roundel with a rectangular banner across the top reading 'PLATFORM' in raised gold, and a large raised gold '9¾' filling the disc. Gold outline throughout. Roughly 35mm.

pins.name: Flying Key / winged key pin (official product name not identified)
pins.property: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED to a product. Depicts the enchanted flying key from the Philosopher's Stone key-chamber sequence (the silver winged key Harry catches). No matching retail listing was found before the search budget ran out. Winged-key designs are also a very common Etsy fan-pin subject, so licensed status is unverified — however the clean gold plating and single-tone pale-blue wing fill are consistent with commercial hard-enamel production.
pins.board_note: Middle of the upper cluster. Gold-plated old-fashioned key seen face-on, ornate bow at the top, shaft pointing down, with a pair of large outstretched pale-blue/turquoise enamel insect-style wings either side of the shaft. Roughly 45mm across the wingspan.

pins.name: Weasley twins / 'WEASLEY' firework pin (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED to a product, and LICENSING IS UNVERIFIED — flagging as a possible unlicensed fan pin. Viewed rotated 90 degrees from how it sits on the board, the design is a mirror-symmetric comet/firework: a six-pointed red star at the tip with a streaking trail, the body split lengthwise into a navy half and a red half, each half carrying a white silhouette of a robed, pointed-hatted wizard aiming a star-tipped wand — i.e. Fred and George mirrored. 'WEASLEY' runs along the seam, printed once forward and once mirror-reversed, which is why it appears backwards in the photo. Searches for this design returned only eBay listings for a differently-designed 'Weasley's Wizard Wheezes Shop Pin' (one of which claims Warner Bros. manufacture) and a large volume of Etsy Fred-and-George fan pins. The chunky die-cut white border and flat matte colour fills here are typical of soft-enamel or printed-acrylic fan production as much as of licensed goods. Do not treat as licensed without seeing the backstamp.
pins.board_note: Upper-right of the Wizarding World cluster, mounted rotated ~90° so the text reads bottom-to-top. Arrow/comet-shaped die-cut with a thick white border; navy and red halves, white wizard silhouettes with star-tipped wands at the wide end, red six-pointed star at the point. Roughly 45mm long.

pins.name: Hogwarts crest shield pin (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED to a specific product. CORRECTION to the collector's own note: this is not a yellow-and-black single-house badge — it is the full four-house Hogwarts crest with all four animals in their house colours. Many licensees sell a near-identical pin (searches surfaced Walmart's 'Harry Potter Monogram Hogwarts Enamel Pin' described as 'the iconic Hogwarts crest representing all four houses', FairyGlen's 'Hogwarts Crest Enamel Pin', and others) and I could not fetch any page to compare artwork, so no name is asserted.
pins.board_note: Centre of the cluster. Gold-outlined quartered shield on black. Upper left red/maroon lion, upper right green serpent, lower left yellow badger, lower right blue eagle, gold 'H' on a small black shield in the centre over a vertical gold sword/bar. Black ribbon banner beneath with 'HOGWARTS' in gold. Roughly 35mm tall.

pins.name: Sorting Hat pin (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED to a product. No matching listing found before the search budget ran out. The design has no lettering and no house branding, which makes text-based product matching unusually hard.
pins.board_note: Right of centre, below the Hogwarts crest. Slumped, creased pointed wizard's hat in glossy brown/russet enamel with a wide floppy brim, no lettering, thin silver-tone outline. Roughly 35mm wide.

pins.name: Knight Bus pin (official product name not identified)
pins.property: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED to a product. The Knight Bus (the purple triple-decker from Prisoner of Azkaban) appears in several licensed pin lines and as a Universal park item, but no matching listing was located. Note the board example is a plain three-tier bus with no lettering or destination board, which limits identification.
pins.board_note: Lower-left area. Glossy violet/purple three-storey double-decker bus in three-quarter front view, three tiers of cream windows with black frames, dark grille and wheels at the bottom. Roughly 30mm tall.

pins.name: The Leaky Cauldron pin (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED to a product. Leading hypothesis is a Wizarding-World-locations pin line: searches surfaced ConQuest Journals' 'Officially Licensed Harry Potter Locations Enamel Pins (3-Pack)' (soft enamel, ~2" x 2", straight post with rubber clutch, described as covering Hogsmeade and Diagon Alley locations with a dangling charm) and a ConQuest Journals directional-sign set that includes Platform 9¾, the Leaky Cauldron, Diagon Alley and the Owl Post — the same four location names that appear on this board. That is suggestive but NOT confirmed: I could not load the ConQuest page to compare artwork, and the board pin is cauldron-shaped with no dangling charm, so it does not obviously match the described 3-pack.
pins.board_note: Right of centre, below the Sorting Hat. Die-cut in the silhouette of a three-legged cauldron with two side handles; black enamel body with a bright silver-tone outline and rim, and 'The Leaky Cauldron' hand-lettered across it in white script over two lines. Roughly 30mm.

pins.name: 'Mischief Managed' footprints pin (official product name not confirmed)
pins.property: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
pins.notes: CORRECTION to the collector's own note: this is not a red banner — it is a pair of overlapping Marauder's-Map footprints. Candidate product: the officially licensed 'Harry Potter Mischief Managed Pin Badge (Enamel)' by Paper House Productions, described as the phrase 'Mischief Managed' in shiny gold metal and hard enamel, approx. 1.5", butterfly clasp, on a 3" x 4" display card. That matches the gold-metal-plus-hard-enamel construction and the wording, but the retailer description does not state that it is footprint-shaped, so the match is unconfirmed. Retail price left null — Paper House pins are inexpensive but I have no confirmed figure.
pins.board_note: Lower centre-right. Two overlapping bare-footprint outlines in raised polished gold with deep maroon enamel fill; 'Mischief' in gold script inside the upper-left footprint and 'Managed' inside the lower-right one. Roughly 35mm wide.

pins.name: Chocolate Frog pin (box and frog) — official product name not confirmed
pins.notes: NOT CONFIRMED to a product; three plausible candidates were surfaced and none could be verified. (1) Universal Orlando's 'Chocolate Frog Pin', described as gold-tone metal with hard enamel fill and a HINGED box plus scented PVC. (2) A two-pin set — 'Enamel Pin Badge Set - Chocolate Frog & Box' from The Shop That Must Not Be Named, and the equivalent 'Chocolate Frog Pin Set of 2' from Elbenwald — in which the frog and the box are separate pins; that retailer describes its box as deep purple and gold, whereas the board example is royal blue and gold/silver. (3) An Amazon-listed 'Wizarding World of Harry Potter Chocolate Frog Hinged Pin'. On the board the frog sits as a distinctly separate raised layer with its own gold outline overlapping the pentagon's right edge, which is consistent EITHER with a single layered/hinged pin OR with two adjacent pins from a set. Cannot resolve from the photo. Also note the collector described this as 'blue/gold pentagon' — confirmed, it is a royal blue pentagon with pale gold/silver Gothic tracery.
pins.board_note: Bottom-right of the cluster. Royal blue pentagon shaped like the Chocolate Frog box, with pale gold/silver Gothic vine tracery around the border, small rosettes in the corners, and 'Chocolate Frog' in white blackletter across the upper half. A separate raised dark chocolate-brown frog with a gold outline sits over the pentagon's right edge, facing right. Roughly 40mm overall.

pins.name: Gryffindor house crest pin (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: CORRECTION to the collector's own note: this is not an 'ornate gold picture-frame pin' — it is a Gryffindor house crest. NOT IDENTIFIED to a product; Gryffindor crest pins are made by very many licensees and unlicensed sellers alike. Searches did surface a Universal Studios 'Hogwarts House Crest Pennants' trading pin set via Hedgehogs Corner, which is one possible family for a house-crest pin of this style, but the board item is a shield rather than a pennant so it does not match that set.
pins.board_note: Bottom-right, directly below the Chocolate Frog pin. Ornate gold shield with heavy scrollwork mantling either side; centre panel split with a maroon field and a checkered pattern behind a rampant gold lion; maroon banner across the bottom with 'GRYFFINDOR' in small gold capitals. Roughly 30mm.

pins.name: 'Hogwarts Alumni' pin (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED to a product. 'Hogwarts Alumni' is a long-running merch slogan; searches returned an Amazon 'Harry Potter Hogwarts Alumni Pinback Button Pin' (a button, not this enamel/printed rectangle) and otherwise unrelated Hogwarts crest pins. The design carries a small trademark symbol after 'HOGWARTS', which points toward licensed rather than fan-made production, but unlicensed sellers frequently copy trademark marks too, so treat licensing as unverified.
pins.board_note: Bottom-left corner of the cluster. White rectangle with rounded corners. 'HOGWARTS' in large black serif capitals, each letter filled with a different house colour/animal motif (visible: a red-pink lion motif in the O/G, a dark stag-like shape in the K/T area, a navy serpent forming the final S), with a small ™ at the upper right. Below, 'ALUMNI' in small black spaced capitals flanked left and right by short maroon-and-navy horizontal stripe bars. Roughly 40mm wide.

pins.name: Hogwarts crest metal banner bookmark with woven gold ribbon (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: IMPORTANT MERGE — this record combines two items the collector listed separately. The 'gold ribbon bookmark with tassel' and the 'large brass/black rectangular Hogwarts crest plaque pin' are ONE object: the woven gold ribbon runs down and terminates exactly at the top edge of the brass banner plate, i.e. it is a metal bookmark with a ribbon tail, pinned to the board with the ribbon folded upward so it does not dangle. The ribbon end is frayed/looped rather than tasselled. NOT IDENTIFIED to a product; no matching listing found. Cast antique-brass construction with a die-cut diagonal-stripe field and a separately raised repoussé crest is typical of licensed UK/EU metal bookmarks, but licensing is unverified. pin_type is a poor fit for a bookmark; '3D' recorded to indicate the raised repoussé crest.
pins.board_note: Largest item on the board, bottom-left, roughly 90mm tall. Antique brass/bronze rectangle with a swallowtail notch cut into the bottom edge, giving a pennant/banner outline. Left half plain matte brass, right half a die-cut field of parallel diagonal stripes. Centred over the join is a large raised repoussé oval Hogwarts crest — mantled shield with crown, 'H' on the centre shield, lion/serpent/badger/eagle around it, motto scroll below. A narrow woven gold ribbon runs upward from the top edge, pinned flat with a pearl-headed pin, ending in a frayed loop.

pins.name: 'Hogwarts Railways' / Platform 9¾ snowflake ornament (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: RECLASSIFIED from the collector's list: this is almost certainly a hanging Christmas ornament, not a pin. It hangs from a red grosgrain ribbon that is pinned to the cork above it with a pearl-headed pin, and it is far larger than the surrounding pins. NOT IDENTIFIED to a product; no matching listing found. Note the wording is 'HOGWARTS RAILWAYS' (plural), not 'Hogwarts Railway' — recorded as read off the photo. pin_type '3D' recorded to indicate the layered metal-plus-enamel construction; the field does not really apply to an ornament.
pins.board_note: Bottom centre-left, roughly 75mm across — the second-largest item. Antique-brass six-armed snowflake with fine crystalline branching and a small round red gem set at the tip of each arm. Mounted at the hub is a dark red enamel ring reading 'HOGWARTS RAILWAYS' in raised letters, encircling a white and navy Platform 9¾ roundel with a banner reading 'PLATFORM' over a black '9¾'. Hangs from a red ribbon pinned above it.

pins.name: 'London to Hogwarts' Hogwarts Express ticket keychain (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: IMPORTANT MERGE — this record combines two items the collector listed separately. The 'framed London to Hogwarts train ticket pin' and the 'metal keyring/ring' are ONE object: the split ring is physically attached through a jump ring at the top of the ticket plate. It is a keychain, not a pin. NOT IDENTIFIED to a product; no matching listing found. The ticket number reads 'No. 257' — recorded as read off the photo; this is printed artwork, not an edition number, and should not be treated as one.
pins.board_note: Left of centre. A brushed-gold split ring (~25mm) pinned with a pearl-headed pin, hanging a rectangular metal plate (~35 x 55mm) with an engraved dentil/rope border. The plate carries a printed grey Hogwarts Express ticket image with 'Platform 9¾' along the top and bottom edges, 'No. 257' at the left, small illegible fine print, and 'LONDON to HOGWARTS' overprinted large in white capitals reading bottom-to-top.

pins.name: Hogwarts crest oval cabochon keychain with suede tassel (official product name not identified)
pins.notes: CORRECTION to the collector's own note: the oval is a full four-house HOGWARTS crest (crowned mantled shield with a gold 'H'), not a Gryffindor crest. NOT IDENTIFIED to a product; no matching listing found. Construction — domed glass/resin cabochon over printed crest artwork in a metal bezel, on a chain with a swivel clip and lobster clasp, plus a suede tassel — is the standard format for fast-fashion licensed bag charms (Primark, Hot Topic, Bioworld and similar) as well as for unlicensed handmade sellers. Licensing unverified.
pins.board_note: Right side of the cluster, hanging vertically ~200mm overall. From the top: a pearl-headed pin, an antique-silver lobster/trigger clasp, a large plain split ring (~35mm), two swivel links, then a navy-blue domed oval cabochon (~30 x 40mm) in a dark metal bezel showing the crowned gold-and-orange Hogwarts crest with a gold 'H'. A long maroon/burgundy suede tassel hangs behind and below the oval.

pins.name: Unidentified embossed Hogwarts crest and parchment pennant piece
pins.notes: NOT IDENTIFIED — cataloguing this only so the board inventory is complete. This is the object the collector described as 'a winged shape and a Marauder's-Map-style scroll' on the large keychain. On close inspection it is not part of the keychain and it is not a winged shape: it is one or possibly two flat pieces lying flat on the cork, largely hidden behind the keychain's chain, oval and tassel. The upper portion is a rust-brown embossed Hogwarts-crest silhouette; the lower portion is a cream/gold aged-parchment swallowtail pennant with faint brown map-like markings. Whether these are one object or two cannot be determined from the photo. Its silhouette closely echoes the antique-brass Hogwarts banner bookmark elsewhere on the board, so a reasonable guess is a second bookmark or banner tag in a different finish — but that is a guess and is recorded as such. Too obscured to research; no listing sought.
pins.board_note: Directly behind and beneath the large tassel keychain on the right of the cluster, mostly occluded. Upper part: rust/terracotta embossed crest-shaped relief with scrollwork. Lower part: cream-and-gold aged-parchment pennant with a swallowtail bottom edge and faint brown blotchy markings, roughly 25mm wide by 70mm long.
